claims: Eid al-Fitr is also known as the "Festival of Breaking the Fast".
Eid al-Fitr is a three-day Islamic holiday.
Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan’s month-long dawn-to-sunset fasting.
Eid al-Fitr is celebrated on the first day of Shawwal.
Eid al-Fitr was established by the Prophet Muhammad.
The festival officially lasts for three days.
The start date of Eid al-Fitr depends on the sighting of the new crescent moon.
Common practices for Eid al-Fitr include wearing new or clean clothes.
Common practices for Eid al-Fitr include performing special morning prayers.
Common practices for Eid al-Fitr include greeting one another with "Eid Mubarak".
Common practices for Eid al-Fitr include giving to charity.
Common practices for Eid al-Fitr include eating sweets.
Eid al-Fitr follows the lunar Hijri calendar.
The date of Eid al-Fitr changes every year.
The date of Eid al-Fitr moves approximately 11 days earlier each time.
Fasting is strictly forbidden on the day of Eid al-Fitr.
